hypotheses.summary: The deploy of revision 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e at 15:13 introduced a latency regression: p95 rose from a 220ms baseline at 15:13 to 900ms at 15:14, 1800ms at 15:15 (onset) and 5000ms timeouts at 15:16. It is the only recorded change to io-shop in the two weeks before the incident, and it lands one minute before the first degraded minute.

supporting_evidence.claim: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-02T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-16T15:20:00Z — only the 15:13 deploy is listed; no other change, no flag toggle.
WARN io-shop: p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline
metrics bucket 2026-09-16T15:13:00Z error_rate 0.01 p95 220 → 15:16:00Z error_rate 0.12 p95 5000, with request_volume flat (1150 → 1050)

hypotheses.summary: No cause is positively identified: the logs only restate the latency symptom and never name a code path, dependency or configuration change, and the deploy record gives no diff or prior revision. The timing correlation with the 15:13 deploy could be coincidental with an unrecorded external cause (e.g. a downstream dependency or database slowdown) — flat request volume with rising latency and timeouts is equally consistent with that.

supporting_evidence.claim: Logs 15:10–15:16:15 contain only 'request succeeded', 'p95 latency climbing', 'p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline', 'request timeout after 5000ms' — no dependency, flag or error detail.
No feature-flag or configuration change appears in any change window read (2026-09-02T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-16T15:20:00Z).
